description: Verify that DUT ingests a 576-octet DHCPOFFER (RFC 791 minimum reassembly / RFC 2131 §2 maximum DHCP message size) and emits the resulting DHCPREQUEST
approach:
[Objective]
576 bytes is the minimum IPv4 datagram size every host must accept un-fragmented (RFC 791 §3.2). RFC 2131 §2 also lists 576 as the legal maximum DHCP message size. This case stresses DUT's ingest with a fully padded OFFER.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. DUT → wire: DHCPDISCOVER.
2. Tester → DUT: DHCPOFFER padded to 576 octets (with End Option + zero pad).
3. DUT → wire: DHCPREQUEST   ← key check (proves DUT successfully parsed the padded OFFER)

[Pass condition]
REQUEST observed after the 576-byte OFFER.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_discover — DUT did not emit DHCPDISCOVER
• Fail_no_request — DUT did not emit DHCPREQUEST after the padded OFFER (parser choked on padding)

verdicts.Pass: DUT parsed 576-byte OFFER and REQUESTed — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_discover: No DUT DHCPDISCOVER within the listen window
verdicts.Fail_no_request: No DUT DHCPREQUEST after the padded OFFER
